chunk_findings.detail: The `locks` view wires the concrete git probe implementation directly in the API surface: `probes=GitProbes(repo) ...` imports `GitProbes` from `ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py` and constructs it there. Under [r-adapters], git is an external dependency that must be reached through a port in `ddflow/adapters`; introducing/using a git probe implementation outside that adapter port couples the API to the concrete git implementation and prevents a fake git probe from being injected through the normal port boundary.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/metrics.py:43

chunk_findings.detail: The new `Probes` protocol and its default `GitProbes` implementation form the git port for this feature, but they live in `ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py` instead of `ddflow/adapters`. [r-adapters] requires every external dependency (explicitly including git) to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, with one implementation per function. As written, the git seam and its default adapter are service-local, so changing or swapping the external git behavior touches the service module rather than the adapter layer, violating the recorded rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py:Probes

chunk_findings.detail: `_declared` decides whether an item is in scope by looking only at `ctx.facts.landings[item][0].at`, while `_merges` filters every landing with `ctx.in_scope(i, m.at)`. Given a window where `ctx.in_scope(item, t)` is true only for `t >= 100`, and `ctx.facts.landings["A"] = [Landing(at=50, ...), Landing(at=150, ...)]`, `_merges` counts the 150 merge, but `_declared` sees the first landing at 50, treats the item as out of scope, and skips it entirely. The declared-item count and both declared shares then omit a merged item that is in scope, and if landing order is not guaranteed the result is order-dependent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/locks.py:_declared

chunk_findings.detail: This change adds the git probe port/implementation (`Probes`, `GitProbes`) under `ddflow/services/metrics` and consumes it in `locks.py` via `from .lockgit import Probes`, rather than placing the port/default adapter in `ddflow/adapters`. That violates the project's adapter guidance [r-adapters], which requires external dependencies such as git to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters` so that swapping or faking git touches one place.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py:GitProbes

chunk_findings.detail: The new lock metrics view imports `Probes` from `ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py` and dispatches `view == "locks"` through it, while `lockgit.py` also provides `GitProbes` (a git-backed implementation). This places a new external-dependency port/adapter outside `ddflow/adapters`, so `ddflow metrics locks` couples the metrics service directly to a service-local git probe rather than to an adapter-layer port/fake, violating [r-adapters].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/service.py:17

chunk_findings.detail: The test file introduces a direct external dependency on the `git` binary by calling `subprocess.run(["git", ...])` in `_git` and then using it to build a real repository in `test_git_probes_read_files_and_conflicts_through_infra_git` (line 185 also imports `GitProbes` from `ddflow.services.metrics.lockgit`, not from a fake adapter). This violates [r-adapters], which requires external dependencies to go through an adapter/port and tests to use fakes rather than subprocesses. Concrete failure: on a machine where the user's global git config sets `commit.gpgsign=true` (or where `git` is not installed), `_git(tmp_path, "commit", "-qm", "base")` at line 189 raises `CalledProcessError` or `FileNotFoundError`, so the test fails even though the ddflow metrics logic under test has not changed. The test should exercise the git port with a fake, or at minimum isolate git configuration and skip when git is unavailable.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lock_metrics.py:174

chunk_findings.detail: The new `GitProbes` reaches the git subprocess through `ddflow.infra.git` (`G.paths` at line 29 and `G.run` at line 35) instead of going through a port in `ddflow/adapters`. Git is explicitly listed in [r-adapters] as an external dependency that must have one adapter implementation under `ddflow/adapters`, so a fake or swap would touch only the adapter. Direct use of `infra.git` ties this service to the real subprocess and violates that advisory.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py:15

chunk_findings.detail: `_declared` decides whether an item is in scope by looking only at `ctx.facts.landings[item][0].at`, the first landing in that item's list. `_merges` in this same module filters and sorts every landing with `ctx.in_scope(i, m.at)`, so out-of-scope landings can exist. If item X has an out-of-scope landing first and a later in-scope landing, `_declared` skips X entirely; meanwhile `_actual` includes all landings without any `in_scope` filter, so out-of-window files can also pollute the declared-vs-written shares.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/locks.py:_declared

chunk_findings.detail: `_declared_of` returns `first.globs` for the first lease of an item and is used both by `_declared` and by `_blockers` for wait classification. If an item has multiple leases with different declared globs, e.g. Lease1 globs=("docs/a.md") and Lease2 globs=("src/b.py"), Lease2's `src/b.py` write is measured as outside Lease1's declared globs, and `_blockers` finds blockers for Lease2 using Lease1's globs. The doc says declared is "how much of a lease's globs" never touched, so the globs must come from the lease attached to that landing/wait, not the first lease ever recorded for the item.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/locks.py:_declared_of

chunk_findings.detail: `new = "\"locks.mode\""` sets the default value to the TOML string `"locks.mode"` including two double-quote characters. The intended default for `metrics.lock_revert_key` is almost certainly the config key `locks.mode` without surrounding quotes. When this knob is applied, the lock metrics report will look up the key `"locks.mode"` (with quotes) instead of `locks.mode`, so the strict-locking switch-back call described in `metrics.md` will not match the real config entry and the report will be wrong under default settings.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.metrics.lock_revert_key.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: `_git` shells out to the real `git` binary with `subprocess.run(["git", ...])`, and `test_git_probes_read_files_and_conflicts_through_infra_git` therefore depends on a live external subprocess rather than going through the `ddflow/adapters` port. This violates [r-adapters], which requires git and subprocess tools to be accessed through an adapter and says tests should use a fake instead of the subprocess. In a sandbox without `git` on PATH the test fails with `FileNotFoundError` even before any ddflow code is exercised.
